--- title: "[markdown_to_latex()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-function}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Parse CommonMark/GFM and render as LaTeX. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/posit-dev/multimark/blob/main/src/multimark/_cmark.py#L348-L474){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python markdown_to_latex( text, *, hardbreaks=False, smart=False, normalize=False, unsafe=False, footnotes=False, extensions=(), width=0, options=0 ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Converts Markdown to LaTeX source suitable for inclusion in a `.tex` document. Inline formatting maps to LaTeX commands (`\textbf{}`, `\emph{}`, `\texttt{}`), headings become sectioning commands (`\section{}`, `\subsection{}`, etc.), and links use `\href{}{}`. The output is a fragment (not a full document): it does not include `\documentclass`, `\begin{document}`, or preamble. You can concatenate it into your own LaTeX document structure. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [text]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The Markdown string to parse and render. Must be a Python `str`. [hardbreaks]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Render soft line breaks as hard breaks (`\\`). By default, this is `False`. [smart]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convert straight quotes to curly quotes, `--` to en-dashes, `---` to em-dashes, and `...` to ellipses. By default, this is `False`. [normalize]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Consolidate adjacent text nodes in the parsed AST. By default, this is `False`. [unsafe]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Allow raw HTML to pass through. Since LaTeX is the target format, raw HTML is typically irrelevant. By default, this is `False`. [footnotes]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Enable footnote syntax parsing. By default, this is `False`. [extensions]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Sequence[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [()
]{.doc-parameter-default} : A sequence of GFM extension names to enable. Valid names are `"table"`, `"strikethrough"`, `"autolink"`, `"tagfilter"`, and `"tasklist"`. [width]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : The column at which to wrap output lines. Set to `0` (the default) to disable line wrapping entirely. A value like `80` produces lines of at most 80 characters where possible. [options]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : An integer bitmask of `Options` flags (e.g., `Options.SMART | Options.UNSAFE`). Merged via OR with any boolean keyword arguments set to `True`. Defaults to `0`. ::: ## Keyword Arguments Vs. Options Flags {.doc-keyword-arguments-vs-options-flags} The boolean keyword arguments (`smart`, `unsafe`, `hardbreaks`, etc.) are convenience shortcuts for the most common `Options` flags. When both styles are provided, they are merged via OR. See `markdown_to_html()` for a detailed explanation. ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The rendered LaTeX string. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Render inline formatting: ::: {#19d00450 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} from multimark import markdown_to_latex markdown_to_latex("**bold** and *italic*") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` '\\textbf{bold} and \\emph{italic}\n' ``` ::: ::: Render a heading: ::: {#8b187a3d .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} markdown_to_latex("# Introduction") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` '\\section{Introduction}\n' ``` ::: ::: Enable line wrapping at 72 columns: ::: {#230ea992 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} long_text = "This is a very long paragraph. " * 10 print(markdown_to_latex(long_text, width=72)) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` This is a very long paragraph. This is a very long paragraph. This is a very long paragraph. This is a very long paragraph. This is a very long paragraph. This is a very long paragraph. This is a very long paragraph. This is a very long paragraph. This is a very long paragraph. This is a very long paragraph. ``` ::: ::: Use smart punctuation for typographic output: ::: {#f317a4df .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} markdown_to_latex('"Hello," she said --- "goodbye."', smart=True) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ``` "``Hello,'' she said --- ``goodbye.''\n" ``` ::: :::
